recABS9cTyYGHFXEG.Body: The Sonic Slider is the flagship tool behind Biofield Tuning itself, a weighted tuning fork hand-tuned to 93.96 Hz, the twelfth harmonic of the Schumann Resonance, Earth's own natural electromagnetic pulse. Its extended handle lets you glide it smoothly across the face, neck, and body, and practitioners and users regularly report support for relaxation, circulation, and nervous system regulation. It's the same fork Chance uses in his own sessions, and a great entry point if you want to bring this work into your own daily routine.

A biofield tuning practitioner, he uses tuning forks to help clients resolve physical symptoms, break negative patterns, and return to energetic coherence.

fields.Core Themes JSON: [{"title": "The Key Bridge, the Eclipse and a Comet Named Pons", "body": "Chance opens with a dream he had the night the Baltimore bridge collapsed: flag football, or as he puts it false flag football, played in a stadium shaped like a crescent. Wann ties the collapse to the eclipse pair, arguing the lunar eclipse of March 25 and the April solar eclipse belong to one cycle, with the sun and moon conjunct Chiron in Aries at the North Node. He notes that Chiron's glyph is a key, that pons is Latin for bridge, that comet Pons-Brooks sat about fifteen degrees away, and that the ship was named the Dali."}, {"title": "Sunbury, Edison and a Seventy Two Year Orbit", "body": "Wann had already scheduled the eclipse as the kickoff for his River and star ceremonies at Sunbury, Pennsylvania, the primary confluence of the Susquehanna, a town whose name he reads as eclipse and where he also watched the 2017 totality. Sunbury is where Thomas Edison built the first three wire distribution of electricity, on September 22, 1883. Wann says Pons-Brooks runs an almost seventy two year orbit, matching one degree of precession, was visible that same year, and changed form on that exact date. Chance adds The Scream and the Krakatoa eruption of August 1883, plus the 1811 New Madrid earthquakes."}, {"title": "Orbs at the 2017 Eclipse and the Surrealist Lineage", "body": "Chance describes watching the 2017 totality in Missouri and seeing luminous beach ball sized white orbs rise from behind his car and from the ground, dancing overhead for about sixty seconds with co-witnesses present, before they merged, split and flew off past the tree line. Wann connects this to surrealism, which he says was far more than an art movement between roughly 1910 and 1930: a philosophy shared by poets, political theorists and philosophers who named a greater reality the super reality, wrote manifestos like the Rosicrucians, and juxtaposed illogical ideas. That practice, he argues, is synchromysticism decades before Jung coined synchronicity."}, {"title": "Chiron Was Only Named in 1977, and Beliefs Are Invisible", "body": "Wann points out that Chiron was discovered in 1977, the same year Apple, Tandy and Texas Instruments shipped personal computers and Star Wars entered the collective imagination, and that its astrological meaning of the wound comes entirely from the astronomer's choice to name it after the centaur. Had the man picked Hercules, Wann says, natal charts since 1977 would read that placement as strength instead. Chance offers the parallel of Pluto's 1930 discovery arriving alongside theories of the unconscious. Wann, who reads charts for a living, frames this as evidence that belief runs like well written code: invisible, unquestioned, and self-fulfilling."}, {"title": "Living in a Mystery Instead of a Model", "body": "Wann argues the paradigm is built on astrology, pointing to zodiacs in the Congress building and the Federal Reserve, and describes stepping outside what he calls the 1260 matrix from Babylon: twelve hours, twelve months, twelve signs, sixty minutes, sixty seconds. His alternative is to align with the largest cycles you can perceive without defining them, since you do not live in a model, you live in a mystery. He describes the system as a parasite that makes the host desire what the parasite wants, uses sugar as the example, and Chance answers with Bastian's wishes in The Never Ending Story."}]
fields.Intro Paragraph 1: Mike Wann of Susquehanna Alchemy returns to Vibe Rant to reflect on the recent cycle of eclipses between the end of March and this week. As the all-time champion of digging up synchromystic connections between world events, personal life, and astrological happenings, this hangout with Mike will be as fun as it is mind-blowing.
